fields.description:
h2. Summary

RHOAI should support ingress sharding so that multi-tenant deployments can isolate inference traffic, dashboard access, and internal component communication onto separate OpenShift router shards. Today all RHOAI routes land on the default ingress controller, which means a spike in model-serving traffic can degrade dashboard and pipeline UI responsiveness for every tenant on the cluster.

h2. Problem Statement

All RHOAI-managed routes (model serving endpoints, dashboard, notebook spawner, pipeline UI, model registry API) are created on the cluster's default IngressController. This causes several problems:

* *Noisy-neighbor inference traffic.* A single tenant running high-throughput batch inference can saturate the default router's connection pool, increasing latency for every other tenant's dashboard and notebook sessions.
* *No network-level tenant isolation.* Regulated industries require that inference endpoints serving sensitive data are not co-located on the same load balancer as administrative UIs. The current architecture cannot satisfy this without manual route surgery.
* *Inability to apply per-shard TLS policies.* Different tenants may require different TLS certificate chains, cipher suites, or mTLS enforcement. A single ingress controller forces a one-size-fits-all TLS configuration.
* *Capacity planning blind spots.* Because all traffic funnels through one router, operators cannot independently scale or monitor the ingress layer for model-serving versus interactive workloads.

h2. Affected Customers

* *Enterprise platform teams* running multi-tenant RHOAI clusters who need traffic isolation between inference, interactive, and administrative workloads
* *Regulated-industry customers* in financial services and healthcare who must demonstrate network-level separation between data-plane inference traffic and control-plane administrative access
* *ML platform operators* responsible for SLA compliance on model-serving latency who need independent scaling and monitoring of inference ingress

h2. Business Justification

* *Multi-tenant production readiness*: Enterprise customers evaluating RHOAI for multi-tenant production use cite ingress isolation as a blocking gap compared to managed alternatives that offer per-workload-type load balancers.
* *Regulatory compliance*: Financial services and healthcare customers require demonstrable network separation between data-plane and control-plane traffic for audit purposes.
* *Operational scalability*: Independent ingress shards allow operators to scale model-serving routers without over-provisioning the administrative ingress path, reducing infrastructure cost.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] RHOAI components can be configured to place routes on named IngressController shards via DSC or DSCI CR fields
* [ ] Model-serving inference routes, dashboard and notebook UI routes, and internal component routes can each target a different ingress shard
* [ ] Per-shard TLS configuration (certificate, cipher suite, mTLS policy) is supported and documented
* [ ] Shard assignment is tenant-aware: routes created for a DataScienceProject inherit the shard configuration of that project's namespace
* [ ] The RHOAI operator validates that referenced IngressController shards exist and reports condition errors when they do not
* [ ] Existing single-ingress deployments continue to work without configuration changes (backward compatibility)

h2. Success Criteria

* Platform operators can isolate inference traffic onto a dedicated router shard, eliminating noisy-neighbor latency impact on dashboard and notebook sessions
* Regulated-industry customers can demonstrate network-level separation between inference and administrative traffic for compliance audits
* Operators can independently monitor and scale ingress capacity per workload type
fields.summary: Support Ingress Sharding for Multi-Tenant RHOAI Deployments
